items.title: 61124_Mario Bauza oral history interview
items.q: He said to me one day, I don't know why you bring this crazy son of a bitch in this band.

ctx.x: the band, and I used to room with Dizzy, you know, keep it close to me all the time because I know -- they call it (inaudible). You know, he was a crazy guy. You can never predict what he was going to do next. But he was a hell of a (inaudible) player.

But right away Chu Berry did like this. He was -- he was too much competition for him then. He was like a child. He said to me one day, I don't know why you bring this crazy son of a bitch in this band. They were already working Teddy Reath's band together. He don't want -- he don't want, say, man, I didn't brought him here. I just (inaudible) to play for me and (inaudible). I don't know why, what you got against this -- no, I don't got nothing against him, but you know what I mean. (Inaudible) this different…

All right. So Dizzy say, you know, one of these days this man going to start playing his tenor, and you going to look for his head, going to be in the middle of the floor, and the saxophone in the band. I said, don't do that. Don't pay no mind. Do your work and play your trumpet. Forget about it. He don't pay you. Calloway going to pay you.
